proof_summary: The vanishing geometric sum for a nontrivial 13th root of unity yields a degree-six polynomial satisfied by \(2\cos(2\pi k/13)\), and the double-angle identity converts it into the reciprocal-root relation for \(4\cos^2(\pi k/13)\). The two monic degree-six polynomials are then identified by their six distinct roots, with the constant term fixing the normalization of the linear factors.
